title: PostgreSQL 18.6: the SET ROLE differential of S7's read rule on 200 seeded worlds has zero disagreements with the matrix; the owner probe catches the bypass without FORCE and agrees with FORCE
records: CL-7.4 and LAB-7.c4: the SET ROLE differential on n fresh worlds on the Bench's PostgreSQL, the owner probe without and with FORCE, the four policy variants, and the pg_class read-back
version_string: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit
verdict_lines: [pg-18.6] PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

outputs.kind: harness result: part 1 specimens with checks, part 2 per-world differential, variants and owner probe

values.server: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

container.network: default bridge, port 5432 published on 127.0.0.1 only

notes: Recorded by W1 follow-up 1 (task_label W1-followup-1); the task field is left out because run@1 accepts only W<n>-S<nn> or W<n>-T<nn> there.

The harness is W0-S08's, unchanged: docs/spikes/W0-S08.md asks W4-T10 to reuse rls-spec.mjs for this run. It connects as the superuser postgres over one node-postgres connection; part 1 runs S7.L4's named specimens on the reference world W0 with 34 checks, part 2 runs, for each of 200 worlds from generateWorld(seed) with seeds 1 to 200, the lesson's differential (SET ROLE u; SELECT set_config('app.user', u, false); SELECT id FROM app.documents) for every user against the matrix that canread() computes in plain code, the four policy variants, and the owner probe (SET ROLE app_owner, the table owner, with app.user set to each user) with NO FORCE and with FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

values.baseline_disagreements sums extra and missing ids over every user of every world under the baseline policies. values.owner_probe.noforce_worlds_with_disagreements counts worlds in which the owner, without FORCE, saw rows the matrix denies (the one world where it did not is the one whose matrix allows every cell); force_disagreements is that sum with FORCE on. values.variants_caught_worlds counts, per variant, the worlds whose differential disagreed. values.readback is part 1's pg_class read-back of relrowsecurity and relforcerowsecurity before and after FORCE (checks P1.04a and P1.13c); the harness does not timestamp the read, so readback.at is the run's started_at.

The server ran in postgres:18@sha256:74935e72241653ca55e0414067e6d8763aceb8a810eb51b452253ec3dcfc4336 with --memory=6g and trust authentication, its port published on 127.0.0.1 only; the recorder waited until docker logs showed "database system is ready to accept connections" twice and pg_isready exited 0, ran the harness with node on the host, and removed the container. Placeholders in argv: <port> is the host port docker chose; <sandbox>/work is the scratch directory the result was written to before it was copied to runs/RUN-pg-rls-differential/. The tab's PGlite rerun (n = 50) is not part of this record; RUN-pglite-rls holds W0-S08's PGlite runs.
